title: Wedding horse songs
hookLine: Guru Ram Das pictures the body as a horse the Lord made, ridden home to the Beloved (Vadhans M4, ang 575)

lines: A GROOM ON A DECORATED HORSE.
cards: A drum, a crowd in bright clothes, and a groom climbing onto a decorated horse while the women of his family sing.
In Punjabi wedding tradition, the songs sung around the groom and his horse have a name: ghorian, horse songs. Family songs, teasing and proud, the kind aunts know by heart.
Guru Ram Das took that wedding song and wrote his own, in Raga Vadhans. Same horse, same joy, same ride to the bride's door. But the rider, the road, and the one waiting at the end all change.

teach.h: A WEDDING SONG CARRIES THE NAME.
teach.b: Here's how his Ghorian open, paraphrased.

teach.h: THE BODY: A HORSE THE LORD MADE.
teach.b: The body is a horse, fashioned by the Lord. Blessed is this human life, received by good fortune. And: this body is the horse on which the Lord is reached.
Meeting the True Guru, songs of joy are sung. Four things happen in those lines. First, the borrowing.
He doesn't invent a new form. He takes a song people already sing at weddings and lets it carry the Name. Second, the horse is the body.
Not a prison, not an enemy to beat into line. A horse the Lord made, a gift received by good fortune. A body is how you get anywhere.
Third, the ride. At a wedding, the groom rides to the bride.

teach.h: THE RIDE HOME TO THE BELOVED.
teach.b: In the hymn, the ride is the soul going home to the Beloved, the Lord. A whole human life becomes the wedding procession, and the body is the horse that carries it there.

teach.h: SONGS OF JOY ON THE WAY.
teach.b: Fourth, the songs of joy, sung on meeting the True Guru.
The ride isn't a grim march. It has music in it, the way a baraat, the groom's wedding procession, does. And the picture is gentle.
A rider who hates the horse doesn't get far. A rider who knows the horse is a gift, feeds it, rests it, and points it the right way, gets to the wedding.

how: Guru Ram Das's Ghorian are sung in kirtan in Raga Vadhans, and Sikh teachers read them as a picture of the human body as a gift for the soul's journey to God.

games.q: you're hearing a wedding horse song in the Guru Granth Sahib. in Guru Ram Das's version, what is the horse?
o: the body, a gift the Lord made, ridden to the Beloved.
pride, which has to be thrown off.
games.why: the body is the horse, fashioned by the Lord; on it the soul rides home to the Beloved.

practice: Check in with the horse, from the feet up through the legs, back, shoulders and jaw: where is it tired, where is it carrying more than it needs to?
Thank it once, plainly, for getting you this far, and let one kind thing for it come to mind, water, a walk, an early night. If you pray, Waheguru can go with each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Ghorian. The wedding horse songs. In Guru Ram Das's hymns in Vadhans, the horse is the body the Lord made, and the ride is the soul's way home. Today's word.

orig.note: horse songs, sung at weddings; Guru Ram Das's hymns of this name sit in Raga Vadhans.

carryVoice: Your line: ride to the beloved. The horse is a gift to look after, not an enemy. I'll be here tomorrow.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Vadhans Mahala 4, Ghorian, Ang 575 (the body is a horse fashioned by the Lord; blessed is human life received by good fortune; this body is the horse on which the Lord is reached; meeting the True Guru, songs of joy are sung)
